definitions.explanation: A large earthen mound built as a tomb for rulers and powerful figures in ancient Japan, dating mainly from the 3rd to 7th centuries. The most distinctive type is the keyhole-shaped mound ({前方後円墳|ぜんぽうこうえんふん}).

examples.japanese: この{古墳|こふん}は{五世紀|ごせいき}のものだ。
examples.english: This burial mound dates from the 5th century.

examples.japanese: {大阪|おおさか}には{世界最大|せかいさいだい}の{古墳|こふん}がある。
examples.english: Osaka has the world's largest burial mound.

examples.japanese: {古墳|こふん}{時代|じだい}には{多|おお}くの{豪族|ごうぞく}が{巨大|きょだい}な{墓|はか}を{築|きず}いた。
examples.english: During the Kofun period, many powerful clans built enormous tombs.

notes:
The {古墳|こふん}{時代|じだい} (Kofun period, c. 250-538 CE) is named after these burial mounds. The most famous is {仁徳天皇陵|にんとくてんのうりょう} in {堺|さかい}, {大阪|おおさか}, the largest keyhole-shaped tomb in the world. Many {古墳|こふん} have been designated as UNESCO World Heritage sites.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{古墳|こふん}{時代|じだい} — the Kofun period
・{前方後円墳|ぜんぽうこうえんふん} — keyhole-shaped burial mound
・{古墳|こふん}{群|ぐん} — a group of burial mounds
・{古墳|こふん}を{発掘|はっくつ}する — to excavate a burial mound
